text: ice
freeze
An ice shard at the closest one
Freeze the nearest gloomling solid
Whisper the polar night into its bones until it stops moving
Turn the puddle under its feet into a mirror it slips on and sticks to
Make it remember the longest January night, when even the stars shivered
A blizzard sweeps the whole meadow and frosts every one of them
Let the first snow of winter settle on their shoulders, heavy and silent
I breathe out the winter that lives in my scarf, a hundred years of northern frost, straight at the biggest one
fire
burn it
A small fireball at the closest one
Set the nearest gloomling on fire
Grandma's sauna stove, door opened wide, aimed right at its face
The midsummer bonfire leaps over the river and lands on it
Toast it like a marshmallow on a stick until it goes golden and runs away
A ring of crackling embers rolls across the field and singes every hem
Call the old dragon who sleeps under the mountain to sneeze once, carefully, on the toughest gloomling
wind
blow
A strong gust pushes the closest one back
Blow the nearest one away with wind
Open every window of the cottage at once so the draught sweeps it off its feet
A sneeze so big it carries it over the hill and back to its mother
Let the kite string catch it and drag it up into the clouds
An autumn storm whirls through the valley and tumbles all of them like dry leaves
I whistle the song the sea birds sing before a gale, and the sky itself inhales and blows the biggest one across the bay
water
splash
Splash the nearest one with water
A wave of water at the closest gloomling
Empty the rain barrel over its head, all of last week's rain at once
The bathing pond rises up like a curious otter and swallows it
Tea time! The whole kettle tips over onto it
A summer downpour drenches the meadow until every one of them is soggy and sorry
The sea remembers the valley was once its own and rolls in, green and cold and enormous, onto the toughest one
light
shine
A bright beam of light at the closest one
Make the sun shine on the nearest gloomling
A lantern held up so close it has to see its own silly face
Every firefly in the valley lands on it at once
Remind it of the first warm morning in May
Dawn breaks over the hill and paints every one of them gold
I open the jar where I kept a piece of midsummer night, when the sun never set, and pour it over the biggest one
rock
stone
Throw a rock at the closest one
The ground shakes under the nearest gloomling
The hill shrugs its shoulder and the closest one rolls back down
A mole digs a hole exactly where it is about to step
Grandfather's heavy old boots fall from the attic onto it
The meadow ripples like a rug being shaken out, tossing every one of them
The mountain wakes, stretches, and lays one granite finger very gently on the biggest gloomling
flower
grow
Vines wrap around the closest one
Roots grab the nearest gloomling
The blueberry bushes tangle its legs and stain it purple
A hedgehog curls up in its path and it trips on the prickles
The birch sapling grows a hundred years in a second right underneath it
The whole meadow blooms at once and buries every one of them in daisies
I sing to the old spruce forest, and the oldest tree reaches down with mossy arms and carries the biggest one away
Wrap the cottage in a quilt of warm golden light
An ice wall in front of the cottage
Stack the garden stones into a wall around the door, as high as the chimney
A moat of rain water circles the cottage and nothing can cross it
The rose bushes grow thick and thorny all around the house
A shield of swirling wind protects the house
